title: Johannesburg’s Infrastructure Crisis Puts South Africa’s Investment at Risk
title_cn: Johannesburg’s Infrastructure Crisis Puts South Africa’s Investment at Risk
summary:
Power cuts, water shortages and crumbling roads are undermining Johannesburg’s economy and threatening its ability to retain businesses and attract investment. Can South Africa’s City of Gold turn itself around? On this episode of Next Africa, Jennifer Zabasajja examines the financial pressures and political instability behind Johannesburg’s decline, and whether upcoming local elections could help change its course.
Business Leadership South Africa CEO Busi Mavuso explains why companies are being forced to work around failing public services. Ninety One founder and CEO Hendrik du Toit discusses the investment needed to rebuild the city, while Eskom CEO Dan Marokane explains how the utility moved from rolling blackouts to excess generating capacity—and why Johannesburg still faces outages. Plus, Bloomberg South Africa Bureau Chief Alex Parker assesses the city’s infrastructure backlog and prospects for recovery. 
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Rep. Issa Says Redistricting Creates More Seats in Play
title_cn: Rep. Issa Says Redistricting Creates More Seats in Play
summary: Rep. Darrell Issa (R-CA) says redistricting could backfire in some states by creating more competitive seats that require significant campaign spending. Issa says Flavio Bolsonaro's departure from Brazil could help settle questions around the country's transition of power, while cautioning that his presence in the US does not necessarily mean he will be allowed to conduct political activity from here. On Israel, Issa says Netanyahu would likely continue an aggressive approach toward Iran, Gaza and southern Lebanon if he remains prime minister during another election cycle. Issa also says Congress should address the debt ceiling during the lame-duck session and expects lawmakers to pass the defense authorization bill on a broadly bipartisan basis. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Rep. Landsman: Ohio Early Vote Looks Strong for Democrats

title: Oren Says Netanyahu Could Benefit From Another Election
title_cn: Oren Says Netanyahu Could Benefit From Another Election
summary: Michael Oren, former Israeli ambassador to the US, says many Israelis are in shock as Gadi Eisenkot's bloc holds a narrow lead over Benjamin Netanyahu's, but cautions that the result could still change as votes are counted. Oren says that if Eisenkot cannot assemble the 61 seats needed to form a government, Israel could face another election while Netanyahu remains prime minister. He says time is working in Netanyahu's favor. Oren says a new prime minister could get a grace period in Washington, but adds that Israel's core security policies would be unlikely to change substantially. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: Fed Day Preview (Podcast)
title_cn: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: Fed Day Preview (Podcast)
summary:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF

The Federal Reserve kicked off a two-day meeting Tuesday after raising interest rates after its previous meeting in September. But as Bloomberg News Federal Reserve and Economy Reporter Enda Curran argues, the Fed is facing its most "confusing" economy yet. Consumer spending is strong, but sentiment is weak, and the economy is experiencing conflicting signals, including high bond yields and slow wage growth.

On today's episode:

Enda Curran, Bloomberg News Federal Reserve and Economy Reporter 
Chris Merrill, CEO at Harrison Street Asset Management
Tim Arndt, CFO at Prologis 
Justina Lee, Bloomberg News Senior Markets Reporter (Source: Bloomberg)
